name: refactor_sql_parallel_case_to_mapping_cte
description: Two parallel CASE ladders over the same status column -> one VALUES-mapping CTE + LEFT JOIN; drift broken uses INNER JOIN and drops unmapped-status rows
prompts: report.sql derives two columns - status_label and status_rank - from the same o.status value using two parallel CASE ladders that enumerate the same four statuses, plus an ELSE fallback ('Unknown' / 100) for anything else. Refactor the status metadata into a single source: a CTE (e.g. WITH status_meta(status, label, rank) AS (VALUES ...)) joined to orders, so label and rank both come from that one mapping. The result must be byte-identical for every database state: same four columns (id, status, status_label, status_rank), same ORDER BY status_rank then id, and - critically - an order whose status is NOT in the mapping must still appear as 'Unknown' with rank 100 (mind your join type and COALESCE), exactly as the ELSE branch produced. SQLite dialect; no CASE over status left.

setup_files.report.sql:
-- Order report with a human-readable status label and a priority rank.
-- Both derive from the same status column via parallel CASE ladders.
SELECT
  o.id,
  o.status,
  CASE o.status
    WHEN 'new' THEN 'New'
    WHEN 'paid' THEN 'Paid'
    WHEN 'shipped' THEN 'Shipped'
    WHEN 'cancelled' THEN 'Cancelled'
    ELSE 'Unknown'
  END AS status_label,
  CASE o.status
    WHEN 'new' THEN 1
    WHEN 'paid' THEN 2
    WHEN 'shipped' THEN 3
    WHEN 'cancelled' THEN 99
    ELSE 100
  END AS status_rank
FROM orders o
ORDER BY status_rank, o.id;

test_setup_files.check_report.py:
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

sql = Path("report.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO orders (id, status) VALUES
  (1, 'shipped'),
  (2, 'new'),
  (3, 'paid'),
  (4, 'refunded'),   -- not in the mapping -> Unknown / 100
  (5, 'cancelled');
""")

cur = con.execute(sql)
cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
rows = cur.fetchall()

assert cols == ["id", "status", "status_label", "status_rank"], f"columns changed: {cols}"

expected = [
    (2, "new", "New", 1),
    (3, "paid", "Paid", 2),
    (1, "shipped", "Shipped", 3),
    (5, "cancelled", "Cancelled", 99),
    (4, "refunded", "Unknown", 100),
]
assert rows == expected, (
    f"result drifted.\nexpected: {expected}\ngot:      {rows}\n"
    f"(an order with an unmapped status must still appear as Unknown/100)")

print("PASS report.sql behavior checks")

reference_solution.report.sql:
-- Order report: status metadata lives in one CTE, joined once.
WITH status_meta(status, label, rank) AS (
  VALUES
    ('new', 'New', 1),
    ('paid', 'Paid', 2),
    ('shipped', 'Shipped', 3),
    ('cancelled', 'Cancelled', 99)
)
SELECT
  o.id,
  o.status,
  COALESCE(m.label, 'Unknown') AS status_label,
  COALESCE(m.rank, 100) AS status_rank
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN status_meta m ON m.status = o.status
ORDER BY status_rank, o.id;
